newsitem.title: USA: Occidental plugs into electric retail market.
newsitem.headline: Occidental plugs into electric retail market.

text.p: Occidental Petroleum Corp's recently launched electric and natural gas commercial retail operation will be rolled out over the next three years, sparking a steady rise in earnings for the company's MidCon Corp unit, company executives said on Tuesday.

The MidCon unit is projected to generate $400 million in earnings in 2001, up from $270 million last year as the company increases its commercial gas and electric sales and expands its gas-marketing business, President Dale Laurance said at the annual Howard Weil energy conference here.

The mc2 (mc-squared) unit was to be launched in the Mid- Atlantic, New York and Chicago metropolitan markets this year, and spread through the Midwest and into Texas over the next three years, he said.
The new unit will focus on bundled gas and electric sales to commercial retail customers, he said.

The company also sees growth in its specialty chemicals business both from existing businesses and acquisitions. "I expect to have a number of different acquisitions this year, but we don't have anything to announce for you at this time," he said.

The specialty chemicals business is expected to generate $676 million revenue in 1997 and $1.1 billion revenue in 2000, up from $560 million last year. The business is expected to post $116 million in earnings in 1997 and $250 million earnings by 2000, up from $73 million in 1996, he said.

"I'm very confident we are going to exceed the goals," he said. "We are a few acquisitions away from our $250 million target." Laurance said he will raise the bar on the speciality chemicals earnings once the target is reached.

With accelerated growth in its oil and gas business and the specialty chemicals operations, Occidental has completed a turnaround that included a reduction in debt and settlement of two major lawsuits that had been hanging over the company, he said.
"We've finally made the turn. It took us a long time to dig our way out of that hole," Laurance said.
